newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Gdansk opens PLN 32 mln airport terminal.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Gdansk opens PLN 32 mln airport terminal.

text.p: The northern Polish port city of Gdansk opened on Wednesday a 32 million zloty modern airport terminal for half a million passengers annually, an airport official said.

Zbigniew Salek, head of PLL Polish Airports company told a news conference the terminal, in which the treasrury has 42 percent, PLL Polish Airports 41 percent and the cities of Gdansk, Gdynia and Sopot 17 percent, would also serve as a backup terminal for Warsaw's Okecie airport.

The Gdansk airport plans to open new connections to Franfurt, London, Stockholm and the Baltics as well as domestic flights to complement the existing 54 weekly flights to Warsaw, Copenhagen, Hamburg and Dresden.
Passenger traffic through Gdansk rose to 178,000 people in 1996 from 167,000 in 1995 and was 11 percent higher in the first half of this year then in the same period of 1996, Salek said.
Air cargo traffic through Gdansk fell to 1,315 tonnes in 1996 against 1,455 in 1995 . It is already 14 percent down in the first half of this year against the same period of 1996.
